thread:
amanda: Heads up - our anomaly detector flagged a weird session stitching pattern for user acct: u-1123. Multiple short-lived sessions across eu-west1 -> us-central within 6m.
raj: seeing it too. IPs look different but session_id reused? that’s odd.
sofia: can you paste the raw auth log line?
amanda: log snippet:
```
2026-02-12T09:12:03Z auth[sso]: user=u-1123 session=abc123 device=fingerprint=E7:4A ip=35.187.x.x action=refresh
2026-02-12T09:15:46Z auth[sso]: user=u-1123 session=abc123 device=fingerprint=3C:B1 ip=34.75.x.x action=refresh
```
dave: session id identical but device fingerprint changed. smells like session token reuse or stolen cookie being replayed after client proxy hops.
amanda: security-bot flagged >5 refreshes + geo hop within 10m -> auto-create incident thread.
security-bot: ALERT: SSO_SESSION_STITCH detected for user=u-1123, score=0.92. Runbook: /runbooks/sso/session-replay.md :eyes:
raj: containment steps - I can revoke the active session_id and force re-auth. Anyone object?
sofia: do it. also block the two IPs temporarily and check for service account activity.
dave: running revoke now:
```
# authctl revoke-session --session abc123 --reason "suspected replay"
OK: session abc123 revoked
```
amanda: done: blocked 35.187.x.x and 34.75.x.x at perimeter. Notified tenant admin via email.
oncall-sre: checked Dedicated infra - no new deploys, no KMS key access spikes. KMS ops show normal rotations at 02:00 UTC.
raj: important: could this be caused by a recent RBAC change for the sso-refresh service account? Any elevated perms granted recently?
sofia: checked audit logs for iam changes: none in last 24h. There was a small policy tweak 3d ago but not related to token minting.
dave: pulled token issuance audit: tokens for u-1123 were minted by the public SSO endpoint only. No service-account mint detected.
amanda: likely stolen refresh cookie replayed after proxying. Next: rotate refresh token issuer signing key if we suspect key compromise. But KMS shows no anomalies.
raj: agree. for now: (1) revoke sessions, (2) force password + MFA reset for u-1123, (3) ship alert to affected customers if scope >1 user.
sofia: I pushed an alert rule tweak to reduce grace for cross-region refreshes: increased sensitivity for session reuse across regions within 15m.
amanda: prepping short post-incident note. TODOs: add additional logging for device fingerprint delta, add test to sim replay, follow up on tenant user email.
oncall-sre: leaving a pointer to evidence bundle: s3://redwood-evidence/incidents/1745003210/ (logs, ip meta, screenshots)
security-bot: INCIDENT: created incident/SE-1745003210. Severity: medium. Suggested postmortem checklist attached.
raj: thanks. final ask - can infra patch the auth edge to reject refreshes if device fingerprint hash changes without new re-auth? would cut these fast.
dave: can do - I’ll open a PR to auth service to enforce fingerprint-on-refresh flag and add a rollout plan (canary -> 10% -> 100%).
sofia: add unit tests and a fallback flag to opt out for legacy clients.
amanda: good work team. I’ll record the incident in the compliance log and schedule a 30-min follow-up tomorrow. :thumbsup:
